name: TX-26
label: Safe R

key_factors: Gill holds a roughly 200-to-1 fundraising advantage ($7.3M vs $32K) with $1.96M banked
District leans Republican by 11 points and Gill is the incumbent
Prediction markets price Gill near 97 percent to win
No polls or expert ratings show any sign of a contest
model.rationale: An incumbent in an R+11 district with an overwhelming financial edge faces a challenger who has barely raised funds, and markets price this near 97 percent Republican; every available signal points to a comfortable Gill win.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or a major influx of Democratic outside spending would be the first sign this is worth revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brandon Gill returns as the incumbent in a North Texas district that leans Republican by eleven points. He has raised about $7.3 million and holds nearly $2 million on hand, while Democrat Steven Shook has raised roughly $32,000 with minimal cash remaining, and a Libertarian is also on the ballot. Prediction markets price Gill's chances near 97 percent, and no general-election polls or expert ratings suggest a competitive race.

The structural picture points firmly to the incumbent: the district's partisan lean, a favorable environment for Republicans, and a vast financial advantage all align. Shook lacks the resources to introduce himself to voters or challenge an established incumbent. The forecast expects Gill to win by a comfortable double-digit margin, with residual uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling rather than any evidence of a genuine contest.
